Telescope 3.1 is about Light (H.264) keeping up with your connection. There's a new Dynamic bitrate that follows your Wi-Fi, Telescope tells you when the stream falls behind and what to try, and a batch of fixes on top of 3.0.

## New

**Dynamic bitrate.** Drag the Light bitrate slider all the way right for Dynamic: the phone sends as much as your connection carries, and lowers it within a second or two when it can't keep up, before the video starts to lag. A short Wi-Fi hiccup doesn't count. It climbs back on its own and settles instead of bouncing. Update the phone app too, since an older one uses Auto instead.

**Higher bitrates.** The Light bitrate slider now goes up to 100 Mbps, up from 30. Auto still stays at most 30 Mbps, and some phones' encoders top out lower.

**"Can't keep up" note.** When frames keep arriving well under the target rate, the Mbps readout turns amber and a note suggests what to try, with a **Switch to Light** button on Heavy or **Switch to Dynamic** on Light. It goes away once the stream catches up, and it stays quiet when the phone's camera is what's slow (like in dim light) rather than the connection.

**FPS dropdown.** FPS is now a dropdown with 15, 24, 25, 30, 48 and 60. Rates the camera doesn't list are grayed out, so a phone that tops out at 30 can't be asked for 60. The graying needs the updated phone app.

## Fixed

- The lens dot could go red while on the telephoto after sliding the zoom back and forth quickly.
- The FPS readout counted repeated frames the desktop sends to keep the webcam alive, so 30 fps from the phone could show as 42. It now counts frames from the phone.
- Light now sets the camera up as a video recording at the FPS you pick, which some phones need before they run 60. Some phone makers still hold other apps to 30; see troubleshooting in the docs.
- A size the phone can't encode on Light (4:3 4K is too much for most phones) now stops with a note to try a lower resolution or FPS, or **Switch to Heavy**. Before, it jumped to Heavy by itself, which at that size can need hundreds of Mbps.
- After Light failed on the phone, falling back to Heavy could fail too because the camera wasn't ready yet. It now waits and tries again.
- You can pick a resolution and FPS while stopped, and the phone starts at it. Before, after a size the phone couldn't do, it kept reopening at that size on every start.
- A setting change that doesn't reach the phone the first time is sent again for a few seconds instead of getting lost.
- When a stream drops, the desktop keeps checking why while it reconnects, so a size the phone can't do still gets its note instead of a silent stop.
- The readout could turn amber on a stream that was fine, when frames arrived in bursts.
- Updates: checking with no internet behind your Wi-Fi now says the check failed instead of "up to date", and a download cut short no longer breaks the desktop updater.
- Tooltips show sooner, wrap long lines, stay put while you hover them, and say less.

Found something broken? Open an issue and paste your **Copy diagnostics** report into it.
